materialsList.label: Beams (6 x 6)
materialsList.why: Heavy timbers on the piers. The floor joists rest on them.

materialsList.label: Framing nails
materialsList.why: Hold the frame together. Bought by weight and used up as you build.

materialsList.label: Pier blocks
materialsList.why: Concrete blocks that keep the wood off the wet ground and carry the weight.

materialsList.label: Posts (4 x 4)
materialsList.why: Short posts that bring each pier up to the level of the beams.

materialsList.label: Floor joists (2 x 8)
materialsList.why: The beams of the floor, 40 cm apart. Closer joists make a stiffer floor.

materialsList.label: Framing nails
materialsList.why: Hold the frame together. Bought by weight and used up as you build.

materialsList.label: Rim joists (2 x 8)
materialsList.why: The boards that close the ends of the floor joists and hold them upright.

materialsList.label: Screws
materialsList.why: Fix the sheets down. Bought by weight and used up as you build.

materialsList.label: Subfloor sheets
materialsList.why: Sheets across the joists. They give you a deck to stand and build on.

materialsList.label: Framing nails
materialsList.why: Hold the frame together. Bought by weight and used up as you build.

materialsList.label: Headers (2 x 6)
materialsList.why: The beam over a door or window. It carries the load above around the opening.

materialsList.label: Studs (2 x 4)
materialsList.why: The uprights inside your walls. They carry the roof down to the floor.

materialsList.label: Wall plates (2 x 4)
materialsList.why: The boards along the bottom and top of each wall. The studs are nailed between them.

materialsList.label: Framing nails
materialsList.why: Hold the frame together. Bought by weight and used up as you build.

materialsList.label: Wall plates (2 x 4)
materialsList.why: The boards along the bottom and top of each wall. The studs are nailed between them.

materialsList.label: Framing nails
materialsList.why: Hold the frame together. Bought by weight and used up as you build.

materialsList.label: Gable studs (2 x 4)
materialsList.why: Short uprights that fill the triangle under the roof at each end.

materialsList.label: Rafters (2 x 6)
materialsList.why: The sloping beams of the roof. They carry rain and snow out to the walls.

materialsList.label: Roof sheets
materialsList.why: Sheets on the rafters. They make the roof one stiff surface for the roofing.

materialsList.label: Screws
materialsList.why: Fix the sheets down. Bought by weight and used up as you build.

materialsList.label: Roof underlayment
materialsList.why: A waterproof layer under the roofing, the second line of defence against leaks.

materialsList.label: Roofing
materialsList.why: The outer skin of the roof. It keeps the water out.

materialsList.label: Screws
materialsList.why: Fix the sheets down. Bought by weight and used up as you build.

materialsList.label: Wall sheathing
materialsList.why: Sheets nailed to the outside of the studs. They stop the frame leaning over in wind.

materialsList.label: Housewrap
materialsList.why: Keeps wind and rain out of the wall while letting damp escape.

materialsList.label: Doors
materialsList.why: A way in that closes. Without it the room is not enclosed.

materialsList.label: Window glass
materialsList.why: Lets light in while keeping the weather out.

materialsList.label: Siding boards
materialsList.why: The boards on the outside. They protect the wall from weather and sun.

materialsList.label: Flooring
materialsList.why: The finished floor you walk on.
